title: Agent Workflows in Finance
answer: Proposal responses, negotiated trades, investment committee memos, comparable company updates and settlement.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Drafting Proposal Responses
children.blurb: Drafting proposal responses in finance covers the use of AI agents to assemble answers to requests for proposals, due diligence questionnaires, and client pitch documents.

children.name: Agent Negotiation in Over-the-Counter Markets
children.blurb: Agent negotiation in over-the-counter markets covers automated software agents that represent buyers, sellers, or dealers in bilateral trading of non-exchange instruments such as bonds, swaps, forwards, and structured products.

children.name: Investment Committee Memos
children.blurb: Investment committee memos are formal documents that summarize a proposed investment, the analysis behind it, and the decision requested from the committee.

children.name: Keeping Comparable Company Sets Current
children.blurb: Keeping comparable company sets current means maintaining a peer group for valuation or benchmarking so that it reflects each company's present business mix, size, geography, and sector.

children.name: Automating Trade Settlement
children.blurb: Automating trade settlement covers the post-trade steps that move a trade from execution to final exchange of cash and securities, including trade matching, confirmation, reconciliation, settlement instruction generation, and exception handling.

sections.body: Agent workflows in finance means software agents that read, draft, check and route financial documents and messages. In proposal responses, AI can assemble prior answers, pull product and pricing details, and flag missing disclosures for a human to review. In over-the-counter markets, agents can parse quote requests, suggest axes, and draft negotiation messages, but final pricing and relationship decisions remain with traders. Investment committee memos can be drafted from data rooms, models and prior minutes, with citations back to source documents. Comparable company updates can be refreshed when filings, earnings or corporate actions change the peer set. Settlement workflows use agents to extract instructions, match trades, and route exceptions to operations teams.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are genuinely automated, especially document assembly, data extraction, and exception routing. Proposal response drafting is often a retrieval and template problem, so agents can produce a strong first draft but still need review for commitments and legal language. OTC negotiation is harder because language is ambiguous, relationships matter, and a wrong quote can be costly, so agents mostly assist rather than close. Investment committee memos are improving as models get better at summarizing filings and models, but they can miss context and overstate confidence. Comparable company maintenance is a data pipeline problem, and the site's 354 merger and acquisition filings and 432 company pages show the volume of source material that must be monitored. Settlement is highly rule bound, yet exceptions, failed trades, and cross border differences keep humans in the loop.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section follow the life of a deal and a trade. Drafting Proposal Responses covers the front end, where agents assemble answers from past proposals and internal knowledge. Agent Negotiation in Over-the-Counter Markets goes deeper into quote requests, counteroffers, and the limits of autonomous bargaining. Investment Committee Memos shows how agents turn diligence, models, and market data into a reviewable document. Keeping Comparable Company Sets Current addresses the ongoing data work of tracking peers, filings, and corporate actions, which is where the site's 354 merger and acquisition filings and 432 company pages become relevant. Automating Trade Settlement closes the loop by moving from agreed terms to instructions, matching, and exception handling, so a reader can move from drafting to negotiation to memo to comps to settlement or jump to the page that matches the workflow they are trying to understand.
